definition: A model architecture that maps one sequence (such as a sentence) to another (such as its translation).
details: The seq2seq model used two recurrent networks — an encoder that reads the input into a vector, and a decoder that generates the output from it — and set the standard for neural machine translation. It established the encoder–decoder pattern that the Transformer later generalized with attention.

explainer.lead: It maps one sequence to another, such as a sentence to its translation. It set the encoder–decoder pattern that the Transformer later generalized with attention.

tiers.eli5: Like a translator who reads the whole sentence first, then writes out the version in another language.
tiers.practitioner: An encoder reads the input into a vector and a decoder generates the output from it. This was the standard for neural machine translation.
tiers.paperLevel: Two recurrent networks: an encoder compressing the input sequence into a vector and a decoder producing the output sequence from it.

explainer.example: English-to-French translation where the encoder reads the English sentence and the decoder emits the French one.

citation.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 27 (NeurIPS)
